# **Guidelines**

The **target audience is other software developers**, and your goal is to teach and explain a relevant ethical and/or technical issue of your choice. 

The main goal of this assessment is to create material specifically for software developers, not the general public. The content should go beyond simply presenting information: it must actively foster understanding, challenge assumptions, and stimulate deeper reflection and further inquiry. It must reveal something that most developers are not aware of. It must grab attention.

You may use a poster template as long as it is referenced appropriately.

Submission Guidelines: All submissions must be shared on Google Drive with **editor rights** with me using my Google account [echancrure@gmail.com](mailto:echancrure@gmail.com). All submissions may be shared with other members of the class later on. Submissions titles must be in the format:

* Surname Name Ethics Poster  
* Surname Name Ethics Video  
* Surname Name Ethics AI

Non-respect of submission guidelines will incur a 10-point reduction in the final mark for this assessment.

A 5-point penalty will be applied to your submission immediately after the deadline if it has not been shared or was modified after the deadline. An additional 5-point penalty will be applied for every subsequent 24-hour period that the submission is late.

*What is a Poster?*

A poster is simply a static, **visual** medium that you use to communicate your ideas. The difference between posters and presentations is that you should let your poster do the ‘talking’; that is, the material presented should convey the essence of your message. **There are many guidelines online on good and bad poster design**. What I am looking for is:

* An effective visual communication artefact. The poster has many images, graphics, etc., that make it interesting, with excellent use of colours and text on the poster. The viewer wants to keep looking at the poster to learn more.  
* Content is novel, referenced, current, significant and relevant to the topic.  
* Skilled selection and synthesis of resources to support the analysis of the ethical issue targeted at software developers.  
* The poster is informative and raises topics for further questions or engagement.  
* The poster communicates its ideas effectively: a viewer of your poster should learn something deep quickly.
